key_insight: A two-stage, data-driven atomistic modeling workflow can capture how amino-silane passivation interacts with hybrid halide perovskite surfaces as coverage increases.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to design and optimize surface passivation strategies that could improve perovskite solar-cell stability and optoelectronic performance.
method: Build a large open training set of diverse metal and hybrid halide perovskite structures (hyP-26).
Fine-tune with a small, specialized dataset for an amino-silane molecule on the perovskite surface.
Use the combined model to simulate coverage-dependent molecular interactions at a mixed-composition halide perovskite surface.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a multistep training pipeline and its application to a mixed-composition surface study, but does not give quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Transfer to experimentally realistic molecule-surface systems may still depend strongly on the quality and coverage of the specialized fine-tuning data.
paper_title: Data-driven atomistic modelling of hybrid halide perovskite passivation
